findings.title: Cleanup progress logged at Error level with full ID list
findings.body: All the new progress/success log statements use `r.log.Error` instead of `r.log.Debug`/`Info`: 'Annotations to clean by time' (line 534), 'cleaned annotations by time' (537), 'Annotations to clean by count' (554), 'cleaned annotations by count' (557), 'Tags to clean' (576) and 'cleaned tags' (579). These fire on every successful batch of every cleanup cycle (and the cycle now runs every minute), so normal operation will continuously emit error-level logs that trigger alerting/noise. Worse, each call logs the entire `ids` slice, which can contain up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` IDs (the new test uses a batch size of 32767), producing enormous log lines and substantial log-storage pressure. These should log at Debug level and log only `len(ids)`, not the full slice. This looks like debugging output left in by accident.

findings.title: Cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The cleanup job interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`, making the entire cleanup suite (temporary files, expired snapshots, dashboard versions, expired images, old annotations, user invites, short URLs, query history) run ten times more often. This change is unrelated to the stated purpose of the PR (avoiding annotation cleanup deadlocks), is not mentioned in the description, and does the opposite of helping: running the annotation deletes far more frequently increases write/lock contention on the annotation tables rather than reducing it. It should be reverted (or, if intentional, justified and validated separately), otherwise production DB load and contention increase by an order of magnitude.
